extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators (researchers) and host institutions preparing ERC grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting ERC Starting, Consolidator, Advanced and Proof of Concept grant proposals, including PI profiles, required proposal elements, page limits, eligibility and detailed evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible additional funding (start-up/equipment/facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to an additional amount (specified per grant type) can be requested in the proposal to cover (a) eligible 'start-up' costs for Principal Investigators moving to the EU or an Associated Country, and/or (b) the purchase of major equipment and/or (c) access to large facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Consolidator, Advanced and other grants the additional funding ceiling is specified (e.g., Advanced: up to EUR 1,000,000). Any additional funding to cover major one-off costs is not subject to pro-rata reduction for projects of shorter duration. All funding requested is assessed during evaluation and must be fully justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidator Grant PI profile (PhD elapsed time)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Principal Investigator shall have been awarded their first PhD over 7 and up to 12 years prior to the publication date of the call for proposals (with possible reductions in certain properly documented circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility rules for reducing the effective elapsed time are set out under 'Eligible Principal Investigator' (career breaks, maternity/paternity, long-term illness etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidator Grant PI independence and maturity
rubrics_metrics.description: A competitive Consolidator Grant PI must have already shown research independence and evidence of maturity (e.g., produced several important publications without participation of their PhD supervisor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected evidence includes significant publications as main author in major international peer-reviewed journals or leading field journals, invited presentations, granted patents, awards/prizes, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early achievements track record (Consolidator) — required list
rubrics_metrics.description: In the proposal the applicant PI should list: (1) publications highlighting ten representative publications (those without the PhD supervisor as co-author) and citation counts (excluding self-citations) if applicable; (2) granted patents (if applicable); (3) invited presentations to internationally established conferences/advanced schools (if applicable); (4) prizes and awards (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are to be included in the 'Track Record' section (2 pages). Provide documentation as applicable; only material within page limits will be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidator Grant PI time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators funded through ERC Consolidator Grants shall spend a minimum 50% of their total working time on the ERC project and a minimum of 50% of their total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI must ensure sufficient time commitment and presence throughout the project to guarantee proper execution. Commitment is a key part of evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant objective requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Grants are designed to support excellent PIs who are established research leaders; applicants must demonstrate the ground-breaking nature, ambition and feasibility of their scientific proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications without a record of significant achievements in the last 10 years are unlikely to succeed; proposals must convincingly show originality and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant PI profile — ten-year benchmark examples
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs are expected to have a track record of significant achievements in the last 10 years, typically matching one or more benchmarks: e.g., 10 publications as senior author in major international journals; or 3 major research monographs (one translated); alternatives include 5 granted patents, 10 invited presentations, 3 research expeditions led by the PI, 3 well-established conferences organised by the PI, international prizes/awards/academy membership, major contributions to launching careers of outstanding researchers, or recognised leadership in industrial innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks are indicative and may be considered individually or in combination. The PI should present achievements in the 'Ten-year track record' section (2 pages) as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten-year track record — required listing (Advanced)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the proposal the applicant PI should list activity over the past 10 years regarding: (1) ten representative publications as senior author (with citation counts); (2) research monographs and translations; (3) granted patents; (4) invited presentations; (5) research expeditions led; (6) organisation of international conferences (steering/organising committee); (7) international prizes/awards/academy memberships; (8) major contributions to early careers of excellent researchers; (9) examples of leadership in industrial innovation or design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If chosen, achievements over a longer period can be considered in specified circumstances; provide clear documentation in the CV/track record. Only material within page limits will be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record extension for career breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: For maternity the track record considered can be extended by 18 months per child born before or during the last ten years; for paternity extended by actual paternity leave taken; for long-term illness, clinical qualification or national service extended by amount of leave taken. The track record considered should not surpass 14 years and six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such extensions must be highlighted in the CV. 'Long-term illness' is defined as over ninety days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant PI time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators funded through ERC Advanced Grants shall spend a minimum 30% of their total working time on the ERC project and a minimum of 50% of their total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with other grants, PIs must ensure sufficient time commitment and presence throughout the project to guarantee execution; commitment is assessed during evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required proposal elements and strict page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposal shall consist of: Extended Synopsis (5 pages); Curriculum Vitae (2 pages); Track Record (2 pages); Scientific Proposal (15 pages); Host Institution Binding Statement of Support; Ethics Review Table; PhD record and supporting documentation for eligibility checking (for Starting and Consolidator Grants only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page limits will be applied strictly. Only material presented within these limits will be evaluated; peer reviewers will not be obliged to read beyond the page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended Synopsis content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Extended Synopsis should be a concise presentation of the full scientific proposal, with particular attention to the ground-breaking nature of the research project and the feasibility of the outlined scientific approach. At step 1 the full scientific proposal is not assessed so all essential information must be covered in the synopsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure the synopsis stands alone for step 1 evaluation and indicates primary and, if relevant, secondary evaluation panels or cross-domain nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum Vitae requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The CV should include standard academic and research record and a succinct 'funding ID' specifying any current research grants and their subject and any on-going applications related to the proposal; research career gaps and/or unconventional paths should be clearly explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear explanation of gaps/unconventional paths ensures fair assessment by panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Proposal content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the scientific and technical aspects of the project, demonstrating the ground-breaking nature of the research, its potential impact and research methodology; indicate fraction of applicant's research effort to be devoted to the project (including working time in EU/Associated Country) and a full estimation of real project cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Scientific Proposal is assessed at step 2; timescales and resource justification are examined as part of feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation procedure — two-step peer review and panel allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A single submission of the full proposal is followed by a two-step evaluation conducted by high level peer review panels (may be assisted by remote referees). At step 1 the extended synopsis and PI's track record and CV will be assessed; at step 2 the complete retained proposals will be assessed. Allocation to panels is based on applicant preference but may be changed with panel chairs' agreement; cross-panel proposals may receive additional reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can request during submission that up to three specific persons should not act as peer reviewers for their proposal (subject to constraints). Panels may invite retained Starting and Consolidator PIs for interview in Brussels at step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence as sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For all ERC frontier research grants, excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation, applied to both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation takes into account phase of PI transition to independence, breaks in career, and unconventional paths; benchmarks and expected minimum working time are also taken into consideration. Projects that are mainly collation/compilation of existing material into databases/editions are unlikely to be considered ground-breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project evaluation — ground‑breaking nature, ambition and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation asks: To what extent does the proposed research address important challenges? To what extent are objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art (novel concepts/approaches, cross-discipline)? To what extent is the proposed research high risk/high gain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These questions assess potential impact and frontier nature; reviewers consider novelty, ambition, interdisciplinarity and transformative potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project evaluation — scientific approach and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent is the outlined scientific approach feasible (based on Extended Synopsis)? To what extent is the proposed research methodology appropriate to achieve the project's goals (based on full Scientific Proposal)? To what extent does the proposal involve development of novel methodology? Are timescales and resources necessary and properly justified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility is judged at step 1 (synopsis) and in detail at step 2 (full proposal). Reviewers examine methodology rigor, novelty of methods, and realism of resource/timescale estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator evaluation — intellectual capacity and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to propose and conduct ground‑breaking research? To what extent does the PI provide evidence of creative independent thinking? To what extent have the achievements typically gone beyond the state-of-the-art?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Advanced grants, also assess leadership in training and advancement of young scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator evaluation — commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the PI demonstrate the level of commitment necessary for project execution and willingness to devote the specified minimum working time (Consolidator: min 50% on project and 50% in EU/Assoc; Advanced: min 30% on project and 50% in EU/Assoc) (based on the full Scientific Proposal)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment is evaluated from the full Scientific Proposal; insufficient time allocation may negatively affect evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism/duplicate proposal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant submits a proposal which coincides, fully or in essence, with a proposal made by another applicant, both the ground‑breaking nature and the PI's capacity to carry it out may be seriously called into question. Plagiarism detection software may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive overlap with other submissions is a serious risk to eligibility/funding; applicants should ensure originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation outcomes and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: At each evaluation step proposals are marked for research project and PI. Step 1 outcomes: (A) pass to step 2; (B) high quality but not pass; (C) not sufficient. Step 2 outcomes: (A) fully meets excellence criterion and recommended for funding if funds available; (B) meets some but not all elements and will not be funded. Proposals are ranked by marks and panel appreciation; funding in priority order by rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receive an evaluation report including ranking range. Applicants may be subject to restrictions on future submissions based on outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Concept (PoC) — relation to ERC-funded project
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of Concept Grants aim to maximise value of ERC-funded research by funding further work to verify innovation potential of ideas arising from ERC-funded projects; they are offered only to PIs whose proposals draw substantially on their ERC-funded research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than one PoC grant may be awarded per ERC-funded project but only one PoC project may be running at any one time for the same ERC project. The PoC must relate clearly to the original ERC project; this relation must be demonstrated in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: PoC eligibility — PI and host institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible PIs: all PIs of an ERC frontier research project that is ongoing or ended less than 12 months before publication date of the call. Host institution must engage the PI for at least the duration of the PoC project and be established in a Member State or Associated Country (or other listed eligible legal entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institution is the applicant legal entity and must provide binding support; ineligible or missing institutional statement can lead to ineligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: PoC maximum grant size, duration and cost rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial contribution up to EUR 150,000 for 18 months (ERC expects most projects to complete within 12 months; signed for 18 months with limited extensions). Union contribution reimburses up to 100% of eligible direct costs plus flat-rate indirect costs up to 25% of total eligible direct costs. Final amount must be justified by actual incurred costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must justify requested funding against the needs of the proposed activity; funding requested will be judged during evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PoC proposal elements and 7-page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: PoC proposals must include: (a) short description of idea to be taken to PoC and relation to ERC-funded project; (b) outline of innovation potential; (c) outline expected economic/societal impact including customer/societal benefits and commercialisation process and competitive analysis and IPR/industry contact plans; (d) plan of activities for establishing feasibility including requested resources and full cost estimation; (e) Ethics Review table. A strict limit of seven pages applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only material within the 7-page limit will be evaluated. Applicants must be concise and ensure all essential information fits the page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: PoC evaluation criteria — threefold: excellence, impact, implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: PoC proposals are evaluated on: 1) Excellence (Innovation potential) — does the activity move research outputs towards early-stage innovation? 2) Impact — expected economic and/or societal benefits, suitability of commercialisation process, competitive analysis, testing and IPR strategy, industry contacts and plans to attract further funding; 3) Quality and efficiency of implementation — sound approach for establishing technical/commercial feasibility, plan of activities vs objectives, project management including risk/contingency, qualified personnel, and justified budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PoC grants are not frontier research grants and may be evaluated against these criteria rather than excellence alone. Each of the three criteria is judged by peer reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: PoC outcome rule — pass/fail majority and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers evaluate each PoC proposal on each of the three criteria on a 'pass/fail' basis. To be considered for funding, proposals must receive a pass mark by a majority of peer reviewers on each of the three evaluation criteria. A proposal failing any criterion will not be ranked nor funded. If budget is insufficient, proposals that pass all three will be ranked according to reviewers' marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary, reviewers may meet as a panel to determine priority for proposals with the same ranking. Demonstrable 'hard' commitments (letters of support) or a solid roadmap for follow-up funding strengthen impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals will be subject to ethics review as with ERC frontier research grants; an Ethics Review Table is a required part of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must complete the Ethics Review Table and ensure compliance with ethical principles; failure to address ethics may affect eligibility or evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disfavoured project types (collation/compilation/databases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects wholly or largely consisting in the collation and compilation of existing material in new databases, editions or collections are unlikely to constitute ground-breaking or 'frontier' research and are therefore unlikely to be recommended for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While such resources may be useful, they are unlikely to meet ERC's excellence criterion unless they demonstrably enable frontier research in new ways.
